tracks.title: Pompa Air Si Mbah
tracks.subject: a man in a Bekasi kontrakan whose second-hand water pump dies every morning right when he is soaped up in the shower, so he runs out in a towel to prime it with a bucket, talks to it like an old grandfather, and his wife times him from the kitchen

tracks.title: Genteng Ketiga dari Kiri
tracks.subject: a young married couple in Cimahi on a Sunday afternoon swapping cracked roof tiles on their kontrakan, she passes the new genteng up the ladder one by one while he, scared of heights, will only keep climbing if she keeps talking to him

tracks.title: Daun di Jok Motor
tracks.subject: an accountant in Jakarta whose odd private hobby is tracing the outline of whichever leaf has landed on his motorbike seat each morning into a notebook, dated, four hundred pages so far, until one morning there is a leaf from a tree that does not grow on his street

tracks.title: Biskuit di Canang
tracks.subject: a young woman in Denpasar whose morning round of placing canang offerings in front of the family shop is followed every day by a skinny brown stray dog who eats the biscuit off each offering, until she starts quietly putting one extra biscuit just for him and names him Kopi

tracks.title: Nona di Atas Toren
tracks.genre: Ambonese pop ballad with steel guitar
tracks.subject: a young woman in Ambon moving into her first kontrakan who finds the house comes with a grey stray cat sleeping on the water tank and a note from the last tenant saying her name is Nona and she likes smoked fish, and slowly the cat becomes hers

tracks.title: Bintang Lima Buat Istri
tracks.subject: a Depok ojek driver who spends his one Sunday off taking his wife out on the same motorbike, giving her the full app-style service (spare helmet, mask, 'sesuai titik ya, Bu?') and at the end giving her five stars out loud

tracks.title: Buku Bon Warung Bu Tini
tracks.genre: Indonesian balada folk with harmonica (Iwan Fals-style)
tracks.subject: the owner of a warung kopi near a Jakarta campus who keeps a dog-eared bon book of students' unpaid kopi and Indomie, reading out their debts every month, then tearing out one page as a gift when a debtor brings his graduation photo

tracks.title: Galon Siapa?
tracks.subject: six tenants of a kost in Jatinangor holding a midnight 'trial' in the hallway over who drank the last glass from the water galon and did not buy a new one, until they find the landlady's cat drinking from the drip tray

tracks.title: Kereta Ekonomi ke Kutoarjo
tracks.subject: a Jakarta man on the economy train to Kutoarjo for Lebaran, going home with his girlfriend for the first time, practising polite Javanese greetings for her family while she corrects his pronunciation and laughs

tracks.title: Batik Kembar Hari Jumat
tracks.genre: keroncong-dangdut fusion with Middle Eastern groove
tracks.subject: an office clerk in Solo who buys a new batik shirt for Batik Friday at a small shop on Jalan Slamet Riyadi, only to discover the shop owner sold the exact same motif to his boss, so every Friday they turn up as twins and the whole floor wants a photo

tracks.title: Lutut Bunyi Krek
tracks.subject: a thirty-one-year-old man in Bekasi whose left knee cracks loudly every time he stands up, so he can never sneak out of a boring meeting, a sleeping baby's room or a cinema without everyone turning to look

tracks.title: Kandang Biru di Jok Belakang
tracks.genre: Indonesian guitar-led male pop love ballad
tracks.subject: a young man in Depok who rides every month with his girlfriend to the vet for her old one-eyed cat, steering the motorbike while she sits behind holding the blue carrier on her lap, and realizes this is the part of the week he waits for

tracks.title: Kursi Dekat Jendela
tracks.subject: a fifteen-year-old in Malang on the first morning of kelas sepuluh who sprints from the school gate to grab the back seat by the window, only to find the girl from his junior high already sitting there with her bag on the other chair, saved for him

tracks.title: Satu Cap Lagi
tracks.subject: an office clerk in Semarang whose only pair of work shoes has been resoled so many times at the same shoe-repair kiosk that his stamp card is one stamp from a free repair, and now he is afraid to walk too carefully

tracks.title: Ko Pu Kaki Kiri
tracks.subject: a young man in Jayapura who secretly practises yospan steps in his kitchen with a broom as his partner so he can dance with Martha at her sister's graduation party, and on the night still starts on the wrong foot until she counts for him

tracks.title: Angsa Bu Kos
tracks.subject: a student in Yogyakarta whose kos landlady keeps a goose that guards the gate and chases him every night he comes home after ten, so he learns to dodge it in a shoulder-shaking dance

tracks.title: Eskalator Blok M
tracks.subject: a woman late every morning who runs up the left side of the long escalator at Blok M MRT station while the same man in a grey jacket always steps aside for her, until one day he runs beside her

tracks.title: Kaki Meja yang Goyang
tracks.subject: a husband who quietly fixes the wobbly leg of the old wooden writing desk his wife refuses to throw away, and pencils both their names under it

tracks.title: Tujuh Mendatar
tracks.subject: a regular at a Medan coffee stall who keeps finding the crossword book on the counter filled in by an unknown stranger in green ink, and starts leaving clues and answers for them

tracks.title: Beringin Kaleng Cat
tracks.subject: a pharmacy cashier in Medan who grows a bonsai banyan from a twig snapped off a roadside tree, in an old paint tin on the pharmacy's back steps, and trims it with nail clippers during breaks
